subject: Confirming demo time for APAC participants - DST and ICS clarification
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@finbridge.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-06T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Demo next week - Tue 9am?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for agreeing to run through Redwood. Would Tue next week at 9am work for a quick 30 minute demo for our team here at FinBridge? We have folks across US and India, so someone may join from Mumbai. When you say 9am, is that Pacific time or Eastern by default for Redwood?

If 9am PT is what you mean then that might be late for our Mumbai folks. If possible can you propose a couple of slots with timezones called out explicitly so we can pick?

Appreciate it,
Anjali
Product Lead, FinBridge

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@finbridge.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-06T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo next week - Tue 9am?

Hi Anjali,

Great question and thanks for flagging. Apologies for the ambiguity. Redwood usually defaults to the sender's locale in calendar invites, so to avoid confusion here are three concrete options with explicit UTC offsets and conversions for common zones. Note that in early February all the listed zones are on standard time (no DST changes yet).

Option 1 
Feb 9, 2027 20:00 UTC
  - PT: Feb 9 12:00 PT (UTC-8)
  - ET: Feb 9 15:00 ET (UTC-5)
  - CET: Feb 9 21:00 CET (UTC+1)
  - IST: Feb 10 01:30 IST (UTC+5:30)

Option 2 
Feb 9, 2027 14:00 UTC  <-- recommended balanced slot
  - PT: Feb 9 06:00 PT (UTC-8)
  - ET: Feb 9 09:00 ET (UTC-5)
  - CET: Feb 9 15:00 CET (UTC+1)
  - IST: Feb 9 19:30 IST (UTC+5:30)

Option 3 
Feb 9, 2027 02:00 UTC
  - PT: Feb 8 18:00 PT (UTC-8)
  - ET: Feb 8 21:00 ET (UTC-5)
  - CET: Feb 9 03:00 CET (UTC+1)
  - IST: Feb 9 07:30 IST (UTC+5:30)

I will draft calendar invites with each option and attach an ics file that uses UTC timestamps and explicit timezone tags so your calendar client can show the correct local time. To be extra safe I will also include the IST time in the invite title when applicable.

If any of these look OK please reply with preferred option and I will send a single confirmed invite and attach the short proposal PDF.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: 415-555-0121

Attachment stubs: invite-options.ics

From: Anjali Rao <anjali@finbridge.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finbridge.com>
Date: 2027-02-07T02:17:00+05:30
Subject: Re: Demo next week - Tue 9am?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the clear options. Option 2 looks best for our team in Mumbai, that 19:30 IST is the sweet spot. One small point of confusion for us - some of our stakeholders read "CET" and sometimes calendar clients show CEST depending on locale. Can you confirm that when you create the invite you will use explicit UTC timestamps and also write out IST in the body?

If you can do that we will accept Option 2. Also please attach the proposal PDF.

Best,
Anjali

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-07T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Demo next week - Tue 9am? - calendar formatting note

Tessa,

Quick internal note before you send the final invite. Good to include the IST text in the invite title as Anjali asked. Also:

- Put UTC as the canonical time in the event description like this line: "Event time: Feb 9 2027 14:00 UTC (Feb 9 19:30 IST, Feb 9 06:00 PT)"
- Add a one-line parenthetical about no DST transitions apply on these dates so participants in Feb are safe
- Do not use shorthand like 9am without timezone in the subject or description

If you want I can create the actual ics file that embeds the TZID so Outlook users see the right local time. Otherwise use the invite-options.ics stub Tessa attached earlier.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Ops

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Thanks for confirming. Per Karthik's suggestion I created a single event and attached a final ics named invite-options.ics. The event is created with canonical UTC time and the description includes explicit conversions and a DST note. Event summary is: FinBridge - Redwood demo Feb 9 14:00 UTC (19:30 IST).

Attachments: finbridge-demo-proposal.pdf, invite-options.ics

See you on Feb 9 at 14:00 UTC.

Best regards,
